Furthermore, the compressor introduced water vapor into the compressed air lines, which became a significant issue when the system required continuous operation to cool the camera. The compressor's inability to provide completely dry air resulted in substantial water volumes accumulating in the compressed air lines. This problem first manifested when the compressed air lines used for a sieving operation began to leak water. Swift action was taken to disconnect the compressed air lines, and a new compressor was sourced. Although the replacement compressor was not class zero, it still introduced water vapor into the system. To address this issue, plans are underway to acquire a new, high-quality compressor capable of providing dry air, ensuring the reliable operation of the system. Usage of Peregrine so far Initial endeavors focused on utilizing stainless steel 316L, but these efforts were temporarily halted upon the realization that the M290 required critical upgrades to ensure optimal lighting conditions. This strategic pause allowed for the necessary enhancements to be implemented, ultimately paving the way for successful operation. More recently, the 20 MP visible wavelength camera has been actively collecting valuable data on a series of titanium builds. A comprehensive history of build data is meticulously documented in Figures 29-34, providing a detailed record of progress and insights gained. Peregrine Machine Learning Training A crucial step in Peregrine's automated phenomenon detection is the creation of a labeled dataset, which serves as the foundation for training the dynamic segmentation convolutional neural network. To achieve this, a planar lack of fusion build was deliberately crafted, as depicted in Figure 35. This controlled environment allows operators to anticipate and identify the types of defects that will arise, as well as pinpoint the specific layers where these defects are most likely to occur. The build file is composed of blocks, each representing a range of skipped layers, from a single layer to ten. While the process can tolerate the occasional skipped layer without compromising the build's integrity, operators expect to observe significant defects when four or more layers are skipped. These defects will be meticulously examined and characterized, providing the essential data for Peregrine's machine learning training. Figure 35: Ti-6Al-4V Planar Lack of Fusion Defects. Future Efforts Subject matter experts will meticulously examine the images and compile a comprehensive machine learning dataset, leveraging Peregrine's capabilities to assign precise labels to each individual pixel in the before and after images.
